name: Texas Sharpshooter
shortDef: Spotting a pattern or 'hit' after the fact and treating it as meaningful.
definition: Sifting through data or events until a cluster or match appears, then treating it as a real pattern or a successful prediction, ignoring that the target was drawn around the hits and that chance alone produces clusters.
howToSpot: Was the pattern predicted beforehand, or found by looking afterward?
How many other patterns, places or variables were checked along the way?
Would a vague prediction have 'come true' whatever happened?
classicExample: A man fires at a barn, then paints a bullseye around the tightest group of holes and calls himself a sharpshooter.
legitimateVersion: Spotting a cluster is a fair starting point. It becomes evidence when the hypothesis is stated in advance and then tested on new data, or when chance is properly accounted for.

contrast.fal_cherry_picking: Cherry picking leaves out unfavorable evidence; the sharpshooter draws the target around whatever cluster turned up after looking.
contrast.fal_false_cause: False cause misreads a genuine correlation as cause; the sharpshooter's 'pattern' may be nothing more than chance found by searching.
